newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Electric committee opposes Hutchison offer.
newsitem.headline: HK Electric committee opposes Hutchison offer.

text.p: An independent committee of Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd told shareholders on Friday to reject Hutchison Whampoa Ltd's general offer for the company, saying the utility was worth more.

As part of a reorganisation of the Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd group, Hutchison Whampoa raised its stake in Hongkong Electric (HKE) to 35.01 percent earlier this month, triggering a mandatory general offer at HK$26.50 a share.

"We concur with the view of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell that the offer undervalues HKE and that the terms of the offer are not fair and reasonable and therefore recommend that independent shareholders should not accept the offer," the committee said.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Hong Kong Ltd is advising the independent board committee on the offer. It said the offer price did not reflect the growth prospects of the group.

Based on a company estimate of 1996 net profit of not less than HK$4.15 billion against HK$4.19 billion in 1995, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said the offer represented a price-to-earnings (PE) multiple of 12.9 times compared with a PE of about 18 times for the Hang Seng blue-chip index.
Hutchison declined to comment on the report. "It is really not appropriate for us to make a comment on the recommendation of the independent advisors," a spokeswoman said.
Analysts said the recommendation came as no surprise. Hutchison was obliged to make a general offer but did not necessarily want to raise its stake any further, they said.

"I think the offer price is deliberately low," said Will Beck, analyst at SocGen-Crosby Securities. "I don't think it was the intention to take up all of Hongkong Electric. No one will expect Hutchison to increase their offer," he said.
The reshuffle of Hong Kong billionaire Li Ka-Shing's flagship business group involved Hutchison buying 7.75 million shares, or 0.38 percent, of Hongkong Electric, pushing its stake to 35.01 percent.
Hutchison has agreed to sell the 35.01 percent stake to Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) in return for 886.21 million new CKI shares.
Hutchison parent Cheung Kong Holdings also agreed to transfer its 70.66 percent CKI stake to Hutchison in return for 349.5 million new Hutchison shares.

"I think Hongkong Electric was used in a whole group restructuring so that in the end, Cheung Kong would end up with more of Hutchison and it used the strong share price of Cheung Kong Infrastructure to buy more Hutchison," said Beck.

Analysts said Hutchison had probably taken advantage of Hongkong Electric's weak price to push its stake through 35 percent, triggering the general offer that would not have to be repeated if it wanted to build up its stake later.
"In the future, if they do want to increase their stake they can do it without a general offer," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research.

"If the prospects for Hongkong Electric become a little bit brighter in the future, the share price will be higher than the current price so it would be more beneficial to do a general offer now," he added.
Merrill Lynch said the offer "could be a smoke screen".
"The slim five percent premium to market could suggest that the group might never have been seriously interested in increasing its stake in HKE beyond 35.01 percent," it said in a recent report.
"I think it is just an exercise to try to push the share price up," said one analyst. "Then they can sell it for more."
Hongkong Electric shares closed Friday at HK$26.80, down HK$0.20.
Hutchison's general offer for Hongkong Electric shares closes at 4 p.m. (0800 GMT) on February 5.
